title: Fractional Impurity Entropy from Potential Scattering in a Free Electron Gas
authors: Syeda Neha Zaidi, Jukka I. Väyrynen
abstract: Fractional changes in entropy are often associated with strong electron correlations or non-Abelian anyons in topological systems. We show that neither condition is necessary -- a system of free electrons on a ring scattering off a repulsive point-like impurity undergoes a $k_B\ln\sqrt 2$ entropy change as the impurity strength is increased. This effect arises from a shift of allowed single-particle momenta from integer quantization to half-integer quantization, induced by the impurity. We show that this fractional entropy change is universal across a broad class of single-particle dispersions, demonstrating that such signatures can arise without strong correlations or topological order.
summary: This theoretical work shows that a simple system of free electrons scattering off an impurity can exhibit a universal fractional entropy change. This effect arises purely from the shift in allowed single-particle momenta from integer to half-integer quantization. The result suggests that such entropy signatures are not exclusively markers for strong correlations or topological order.
main_problem: To demonstrate that fractional entropy changes can occur in simple, non-interacting systems (free electrons) without invoking strong electron correlations or topological order.
main_result: The system exhibits a universal entropy change of $- rac{1}{2}\ln 2$ when the impurity strength is varied, which is attributed to a shift in single-particle momentum quantization from integer to half-integer values.
method: The entropy is calculated by analyzing the impurity partition function, $Z_{	ext{imp}}(\alpha) = Z(\alpha) / Z(0)$, and taking its derivative with respect to temperature.
model_or_system: The model is a free electron gas confined to a one-dimensional ring of circumference L, scattering off a repulsive point-like impurity of strength $\alpha$. The analysis compares spectra quantized by odd versus even integers.
key_observables: Impurity entropy change ($S_{	ext{imp}}$) and the boundary entropy change ($\Delta S$).
important_parameters: Temperature ($T$), impurity strength ($\alpha$), and the ratio of energy scales ($\epsilon_\alpha/T$ and $\epsilon_0/T$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on asymptotic limits (weak/strong scattering) and approximations like Taylor expansions and integral conversions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the shift of allowed momenta from integer to half-integer quantization, and numerically evaluate the entropy change as a function of the impurity strength ratio.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the physical model and calculates the entropy change in the presence of an impurity. It then generalizes the analysis by comparing spectra quantized by odd versus even integers to derive a universal boundary entropy change, $\Delta S$.
why_interesting: The finding suggests that signatures previously thought to require exotic physics (like non-Abelian anyons) can arise from simple boundary conditions or level quantization shifts, broadening the scope of what constitutes an 'entropic signature'.
